extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency standards managers, CIOs, policy makers, and NIST/ICSP members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended practices for Federal agencies on participating in, adopting, tracking, and reporting use of voluntary consensus standards under the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119. Covers policy elements, staffing, tracking systems, coordination, and criteria for when to use government-unique versus voluntary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen implementation of NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal agencies should continue to strengthen their efforts to implement the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119, particularly in planning for resource and staff allocation for participation in appropriate voluntary consensus standard activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and allocate resources and staff specifically for standards participation; monitor and maintain progress over time; treat implementation as an ongoing agency priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use voluntary consensus standards where appropriate (procurement and regulatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Federal agencies have continued to make progress in their use of voluntary consensus standards for agency programs and missions. This trend should be continued for both procurement and regulatory activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer voluntary consensus standards for procurement and regulation when suitable; review opportunities to substitute voluntary standards for government-unique standards; document substitutions and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form strategic alliances and teaming with Standards Development Organizations (SDOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, strategic alliances and teaming arrangements by Federal agencies with standards development organizations may be beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue partnerships with national and international SDOs to influence and align standards development with agency needs; leverage industry and academic expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop agency-specific policy and programmatic elements to support A-119
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should continue to develop specific policy and programmatic elements to support the implementation of the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements for consideration include establishment of agency standards policy and units for monitoring standards activities, resource allocation, infrastructure, reporting, and assessing program effectiveness (use NIST policy as a possible model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider strategic agency needs when planning participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider their own strategic needs when planning for agency participation in standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available resources (including NIST) to determine applicable SDOs (national and international), relevant voluntary standards, and the need for new standards for emerging technologies and processes; align participation with strategic mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare staff for standards participation and coordinate positions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICSP should develop guidelines for use by agencies in preparing their staff for participation in standards-related activities. These guidelines ... should reflect the need to prepare agency views and coordinate positions with other relevant Federal agencies so that all Federal needs are reflected as standards are developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train staff to articulate agency views, coordinate interagency positions prior to committee engagement, and prepare for committee roles; use NIST Policy on Voluntary Standards as a model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid appearance of dominance in standards committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration should be given to the appropriate agency role in committee activities to avoid the appearance of dominance and consideration of likely future agency and national needs during the development and revision of voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When participating, limit actions that could be perceived as dominating a committee; seek consensus-building approaches and coordinate with other agencies to reflect broad Federal interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use systems to track adoption/reference of voluntary standards and participation levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should continue to develop, improve and utilize systems for tracking the adoption or referencing of voluntary standards, as well as the level of staff participation in voluntary standards developing bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tracking systems (databases) that capture which voluntary standards are adopted or referenced, who participates on committees, and participation intensity; use electronic tools for directories and information exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use electronic directories and information exchange for standards participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider the use of electronic means for setting up directory databases of participants and exchanging information about standards-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy online directories, shared databases and electronic communication channels to coordinate participation, share positions, and track standards activity across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIST facilitation and information services
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST should continue to facilitate interactions between agencies and voluntary standards process and consider developing a newsletter and WEB-site to periodically provide current information about Federal agency standardization activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage NIST as a facilitator and information hub (NCSCI, SAMI); expect NIST to provide consolidated updates, translations, reference materials, and outreach (e.g., newsletter, website, hotlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting requirements and data to collect (methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare this report, OCIO sought information from USDA Agency Heads based on NIST requirements: number of agency employees engaged in voluntary consensus standards-developing bodies and the number of such bodies; the number of voluntary consensus standards used since October 1, 1997; the number of voluntary consensus standards substituted for government-unique standards in FY 1998; an evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 and recommendations for changes; and identification of all instances when the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards (including rationale and specific standard used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should collect and report these specific metrics annually to NIST/OCIO to fulfill Circular A-119 reporting; maintain records of substitutions and rationales for governmental-unique usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use voluntary consensus standards for items normally procured commercially
rubrics_metrics.description: As set forth in existing DoD policies, items or materials that are normally procured using a voluntary standard by commercial firms, DoD activities also should be using a voluntary standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer voluntary standards for dual-use/commercial items; proactively search for voluntary standard replacements for government documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for retaining government-unique (military-unique) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relies on military specifications and standards in lieu of voluntary standards when the requirement can be justified as truly military-unique; when a voluntary standard does not exist and development is not imminent; when there is no industry interest to develop a voluntary standard to address DoD requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain government-unique specifications only when justified by unique mission needs, lack of existing voluntary alternatives, or no prospect of voluntary development; document justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: MilSpec reform: review and replace where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: One aspect of the Department’s MilSpec Reform initiative continues to be the replacement of military specifications and standards with voluntary standards wherever there is a dual-use application. The Department completed a review of its 30,000+ military specifications and standards to determine whether a replacement voluntary standard already existed or whether one could be developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic reviews of government specifications to identify candidates for replacement by voluntary standards; work with industry and SDOs to plan replacements where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of commercial/industry standards for testing and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: ANSI and ASTM standards are used for most testings and analyses conducted by AMS in providing certification services to the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available and appropriate, adopt established commercial test standards (e.g., ANSI, ASTM) for agency testing and certification rather than creating bespoke government-only methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: When commercial standards fail to meet program-specific requirements, set case-by-case specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: When commercial standards fail to meet the nutritional requirements of the School Lunch and feeding programs, AMS sets specifications on the fat, salt and sugar contents ... they are not coded permanently as government-unique standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where voluntary or commercial standards do not meet specific programmatic needs, set tailored specifications within procurements or contracts on a case-by-case basis rather than establishing permanent government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and document interagency and international coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards that apply to many NOAA activities are established with other Federal agencies ... and through participation in international organizations such as the World Meteorological Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate standards development with other agencies and international bodies where standards cross agency or national boundaries; document coordination and align U.S. positions in international fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain directories and encourage employee reporting of participation (SAMI/NCSCI use)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards Assistance and Management Information (SAMI) project collects and disseminates information on DOC staff participation ... a directory, published annually, contains statistics on standards committee participation, alphabetical listings of staff participants and standards organizations and committees. Department employees are encouraged to provide the SAMI office with additional information concerning participation in standards activities not already included in the directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and contribute to central directories of standards participation; encourage staff to report committee memberships and activities so agencies can track participation and institutional knowledge.
